profile.address: 1111 Comstock Street, Santa Clara County, CA
profile.reading: Prime Santa Clara sits at 1111 Comstock Street in Santa Clara County, California, internally coded SJC02 by the operator, one of three separate buildings that make up Prime Data Centers Silicon Valley portfolio in this dataset. Per Prime own site, SJC02 is designed for 9 megawatts of capacity across 123,000 square feet and is listed as powered shell status, meaning the building and electrical infrastructure are in place without a completed tenant fit-out. Prime own Silicon Valley locations page describes the broader portfolio there as five buildings totaling 57 megawatts, 540,000 square feet, and 17 data halls across 13 acres, of which SJC02 is one component alongside the separately mapped SJC04 building roughly 150 meters away on the same street, and SJC03 about a kilometer away on Martin Avenue. No tenant is disclosed for SJC02, and no year-built figure is published. Prime Data Centers was founded in 2017 in California and is now headquartered at 400 North Ervay Street in Dallas, Texas. The company describes itself on its own site as majority founder-owned, a description that does not claim institutional private equity or infrastructure fund majority ownership, though it does not rule out unnamed minority capital partners either. Founder and CEO Nicholas Laag leads the company alongside CFO Ulrich Pelz and other named executives. Prime describes its overall footprint as 28 data centers across 13 campuses with a stated pipeline exceeding 4 gigawatts, spanning Austin, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Sacramento, and Silicon Valley in North America, plus Frankfurt and Madrid in Europe and a newly announced site in Esbjerg, Denmark. Santa Clara sits at the heart of Silicon Valley, one of the most constrained and expensive data center land and power markets in the country, a dynamic reflected in Prime decision to develop a multi-building, phased portfolio there rather than one single large campus.

reading.body:
Prime Santa Clara publishes 57 MW of IT capacity across 540,000 square feet of technical space at 26415 Corporate Ave in Santa Clara County. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 57 MW of IT load is roughly 1,425 racks, and at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, it is roughly 5,700 racks. Those two figures bracket the plausible range; which end applies depends on the workload mix, which the operator does not publish.

The three certifications define what the campus is qualified to host. SOC 2 Type 2 means the operator's controls over security, availability, and related trust criteria have been audited by an independent party over a sustained period. PCI DSS means the facility meets the payment card industry's physical and logical security requirements for handling cardholder data. ISO 27001 means an accredited body has certified the information security management system against that international standard. Together, the certifications qualify the campus for regulated and payment-sensitive workloads, but which tenants have chosen it is not published.

This site has mapped 103 data center facilities in California, of which 10 have published a megawatt figure on their operator spec pages. Those 10 sum to 356 MW of published IT capacity. At 57 MW, Prime Santa Clara represents roughly 16 percent of that published total, and it ranks third among the facilities for which this site holds a comparable number. That rank reflects only what operators have chosen to publish, not the full installed base of the state.
